source_used: Governing (MassLive column by Scott Kirsner via TNS)
key_facts: Massachusetts may be on the verge of passing one of the country's most stringent AI safety laws
Gov. Maura Healey asked legislators to add AI safety and transparency language to the Mass Wins economic development bill
California, Illinois and New York already require big developers to publish risk plans and report incidents; Illinois requires annual third-party audits
The Massachusetts proposal would have independent evaluators test models for catastrophic risk at least three times a year, paid by the developers
Applies to developers with more than $500 million in annual revenue
Committee chair Sen. Barry Finegold said the issue was "still being discussed"
Anthropic and OpenAI say they support independent evaluations; Trump favours industry self-regulation
quote_evidence: Massachusetts may be on the verge of passing one of the country’s most stringent AI safety laws, putting the state on a collision course with President Donald Trump’s hands-off approach to rapidly evolving technology.
But the first-in-the-nation concept of independent evaluators examining AI models isn’t a done deal.
why_it_matters_hint: A state may require outside testing of AI models, going beyond other state laws.
title: Massachusetts Could Set a New Standard for AI Safety
